assign.request: (1) The every-prompt skill stays minimal and re-reads on every prompt; long detail moves to sub-readmes it names with 'load this if you need X'. A separate MASTER ASSISTANT skill that only supervises and knows what is going on: the fast assistant can ask it for feedback and it replies with opinions, does no heavy work, documents the whole process on a page, and doubles as the system auditor. (3) Assistants do no deep reasoning: they sort, log everything loggable, and relay each prompt to the proper independent mastermind, which does the deep work and spawns minions in parallel. Build this into the right skill roles.

steps: Read every-prompt/SKILL.md in full so nothing is lost

decision.about: does the auditor become a section of master-assistant, or a skill master-assistant loads when an audit is asked for?

options.say: keep `auditor` its own small skill; master-assistant says: when a mistake reaches the owner or a judgment call turns out wrong, load `auditor` and follow it. Two small skills, one role wearing both.
fold the auditor's procedure into master-assistant as a section

decision.because: the two jobs have opposite shapes. Supervision is what the master assistant does all day and must stay cheap to re-read; an audit is rare, long, and changes on its own evidence (it already carries a reading list, a ranking rule, a note format and a stop rule - 81 lines, and it grows with each audit). Folding them makes the everyday skill three times heavier for a job done a few times a week, and every future audit lesson would fatten the file the supervisor re-reads. Loading is one call with its own context, and it keeps the auditor usable by anyone else the mastermind spawns - which is how it was used four times today.
decision.alternative_cost: one extra Skill call at the start of an audit, and two files to keep honest instead of one
decision.status: applied - master-assistant says to load it

decision.about: which model runs the master assistant - the owner said Fable, and the weekly budget line was hit today

options.say: Opus by default; Fable only for an architecture question - a role boundary, a skill rewrite, a system-shaped judgment call

decision.because: the master assistant's everyday work is reading state and giving a two-sentence opinion, which Opus does at a fraction of the cost, and the weekly line was hit today. The jobs that genuinely want Fable are rare and identifiable - the ones where being wrong reshapes how everything else runs. Recommendation, not a decision taken: the owner said Fable, so this is theirs to confirm.
decision.alternative_cost: an Opus opinion on an architecture question is worse than a Fable one - which is why the carve-out exists rather than a flat downgrade

log.msg: The heredoc trap bit me mid-task, in the same session in which I wrote the skill line about it: a `python - <<PY` block hung waiting on stdin and had to be backgrounded, and the edits were done with the Edit tool instead. Third occurrence in two days across three different agents. This is more evidence for the incident audit's change 2 - the harness traps belong in CLAUDE.md, the one file every agent reads, because knowing the rule and having written it down is demonstrably not enough.

assign.outcome:
**The fast assistant's skill is now a 43-line core it can afford to re-read every prompt, and a master assistant exists to supervise, opine and audit.** [/framework/ai/2026-09-19/skill-roles/](/framework/ai/2026-09-19/skill-roles/)

**`every-prompt/SKILL.md`: 128 → 43 lines** (36 of body) — who you are, the two commands in order (`heard` unless the prompt carries the hook's `prompt-relay:` note, then `say` with `--id/--icon/--status/--re`), the doorbell, routing, what you never do, and a **load this if…** list. Nothing was dropped; it moved to four sub-readmes beside it: **`cards.md`** (the dashboard card craft), **`headless.md`** (the server-spawned mode), **`tiers.md`** (the roles table), **`trouble.md`** (relay not delivered, the echo hook, quoting).

**`master-assistant/SKILL.md`, 52 lines** — supervises from `say.mjs state`, the board and the task logs; answers the fast assistant or the mastermind in **one or two sentences of opinion** and stops; keeps one page current on how the process itself is going (`public/framework/ai/process/` — the spec is in the skill, the first version is on this task's page); and **loads `auditor`** when a mistake or a wrong judgment call arrives.

**Two decisions** (both `decision` lines with their alternatives): the **auditor stays its own skill** — supervision is everyday and must stay cheap to re-read, an audit is rare, long and grows with its own evidence, so two small skills, one role wearing both. **Model: Opus, with Fable for architecture questions** (role boundaries, skill rewrites, system-shaped judgment calls) — the owner said Fable and the weekly line was hit today, so this one is theirs to confirm.

**Five contradictions for the mastermind to fix in its own file** (listed as cards on the page, not edited): it still calls the skill `assistant`; "post first, work second" now races the fast tier for the same card (the mastermind's job is to REFINE under the same id); the fast tier reads as optional when it is not; the master assistant does not exist there at all; and nothing says how routing works when several masterminds run — the smallest fix is a `masterminds` list in the ledger that `state` prints.

**Skill text: 2,593 → 2,667 lines.** The whole gain is the new role; the number that matters went the other way — the only file re-read on every prompt is now a third of its old size.
